properties.statement:
REFLOW2 COMPUTES WHETHER A DESIGN IS DELIVERING AND ITS INSTRUCTION SURFACE NEVER ROUTES ANYONE THERE. Found 2026-08-29 when Anthony challenged a claim this session had made — that "nothing in the orientation reads measures whether reflow2 does what it's supposed to do". THE CLAIM WAS FALSE ABOUT THE TOOL AND TRUE ABOUT THE EXPERIENCE, and the gap between those two is the defect.

═══ ① THE MEASURE EXISTS, AND IS PROMINENT ═══

`graph_report_markdown` returns, in its seventh line: *"Delivered: 151 of 193 requirement(s) (158 satisfied) — computed from the thread (something satisfies it, and that capability is built and currently passing), not from a status field."* That is exactly the answer to "does my project do what it is supposed to do", computed rather than asserted. NINE report functions in core answer that family of question: coverage, evidence, maturity, readiness, consumption, ility, flow, graph, forecast_readiness.

THIS SESSION READ THAT LINE AT ORIENTATION, never mentioned it again, and four hours later computed the same number by hand in Python to answer the same question. That is the symptom, and the agent was not being careless.

═══ 🛑 ② THE MEASURED CAUSE: THE INSTRUCTION SURFACE IS HYGIENE-WEIGHTED ═══

Named in the 23 served skills:

    detect_gaps            16 of 23      hygiene
    loop_status            12 of 23      hygiene
    coverage_report         5 of 23
    graph_report            3 of 23
    seam_report             2 of 23
    evidence_report         1 of 23
    maturity_report         0 of 23      <-- and 0 instruction files
    readiness_report        0 of 23      <--
    consumption_report      0 of 23      <--
    ility_report            0 of 23      <--
    forecast_readiness      0 of 23      <--

Also checked, because a skill is not the only surface: NONE of the evaluative reports is named in `AGENTS.md` or in `service.rs` either. They are reachable only by an agent that goes looking through the raw tool list.

⭐ AND THE ORIENTATION SKILL IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE. `where-am-i` GATHERS `graph_report_markdown` — so the delivery line is in the agent's hands — and then its "Tell them" section gives EIGHT numbered steps of what to say, none of which is how much of the intent is actually built and working. The words "deliver", "coverage" and "satisfied" appear ZERO times in that skill. An agent that follows the script faithfully reports what is undecided and never reports what is done.

═══ ③ THE CLASS, and it is the same one three other findings describe ═══

Built, correct, and not routed. `cap:built-and-consumed-by-nothing` is a detector for exactly this shape. The linking layer (`mirror_surface`, `export_surface`, `pair_designs`, `seam_report`) was measured at ZERO instances while being built and verified. And the 2026-08-29 skill-adoption measurement across 93 sessions found that what predicts a skill's load count is being named in an ALWAYS-INJECTED SURFACE, not being in the served catalogue — which is this fact stated about skills instead of about reports.

⚠️ WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A MISSING MENTION: it makes reflow2 PRESENT AS a hygiene server to the person using it. A user asking "is my project doing what it is supposed to do" is answered with gaps, defects and export sync — not because the tool cannot answer, but because nothing tells the agent to ask the half that can.

🛑 NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the five zero-mention reports are actually UNUSED in the field, or merely unmentioned. Naming was measured; invocation was not. The 93-session measurement is suggestive for skills and does not transfer to tools without its own count. Also not established: whether `Delivered: N of M` is the right headline for a USER's project rather than for reflow2's own — it is computed from the thread, so it measures whether the design's own chain is complete and its recorded checks pass, which is a narrower claim than "the system works".
